items.html: And if you should ask, the Partzuf of Aba does not finish descending until a third of Tifferet, as above. It may be said that that third of Tifferet is to Aba in the aspect of Yesod, and it is like ZA with his Mochin from the side of Bina. And you must understand this whole matter according to that same matter, all in a single image, and then you will understand it. Now Yesod as a whole is the aspect of front, and it has no posterior that descends from it. This is unlike the rest of the Guf, which has an aspect of posterior that faces the front of the female, but whose posterior is not attached to her. Therefore the end of the posterior of Aba finishes descending before there was a flaw and deficiency in the Yesod of Aba. Afterward, the third king, who is Gevura, died, and drew the expansion of the five Gevurot into Ima Ila'ah. And when he died he descended to Beria, and the four lights descended into the fourth vessel, which is Tifferet; then the expansion of the Gevurot fell into the Yesod of Ima, and her posterior also fell downward. Then Ima too turned back her posterior, and the posterior of Ima was against the posterior of Aba.
